item.title: Re: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Agreeing with Hexick's post above, and noting that if you're looking to work on your writing skills specific to SCP articles, you don't necessarily need to ask for feedback on a whole draft. If you're seeking to improve clinical tone, for example, you can post short excerpts in the Questions Desk forum to ask for opinions on what to improve. You can also ask for tips on writing certain parts of an SCP article, such as interviews. Examples of such threads include:

  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13834538/dialogue-and-interviews
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13787438/references-for-ideas-on-interactions-between-foundation-and
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13696555/containment-procedure-required
  • http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13695935/how-much-is-too-much-detail

Oftentimes a draft isn't interesting to a reviewer because the core concept is boring/unwieldy. If you're going to ask someone to review an entire sandbox draft, ideally you'd have an interesting concept written up and not just a throwaway practice premise that might introduce issues that will distract a reviewer from focusing on the writing separate from the concept.

item.title: Re: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Greenlights, while highly recommended for first-time authors, are only required to post in the Draft Critique Forum, and are obtained via concept threads in the Ideas Forum.

Additionally, another way of receiving critique is through the #thecritters chatroom on our IRC network (SkipIRC | irc.scpwiki.com | SSL Port: 6697), which while it doesn't require greenlights to get feedback there, some reviewers may refuse to look at drafts for new writers who haven't already gotten greenlights in the forums. If you want to head over there, make sure to read the Chat Guide I previously linked, and either way, I strongly recommend you go through the greenlight process in addition.

item.title: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Soo, I didn't really want to put my concept in the Ideas and Brainstorming forum yet, because I wanted to improve my writing.

Is there any way I could get a feedback from a reviewer or crit team to review my sandbox?
